description:
## Question

How does a consumer deploy and assemble the building blocks?

## Context

Map turnkey-wit: turnkey is a Nix flake framework (flake-parts + devenv modules); consumers are turnkey-managed repos on GitHub; GCP first; scale to zero; every artifact should be reproducible (images built by Nix). Depends on "What are the building blocks…".

## Decide (grilling)

1. Infrastructure-as-code vehicle for GCP resources: OpenTofu/Terraform modules shipped by turnkey, generated from Nix (terranix), gcloud scripts, or something else; how it stays provider-swappable.
2. How service images are built (nix2container / dockerTools) and published (registry, tags pinned to turnkey revision — cf. ADR 0002's "pin together, bump together").
3. How the consumer's flake/turnkey options connect to a deployment (endpoint, keys, public/private repo) — flake-parts options vs a separate "infra" flake output.
4. GitHub App installation and secret-free bootstrap; upgrade path when turnkey bumps.
5. What a new consumer does end to end (a checklist the user manual will carry).

## Output

Resolution comment; `docs/specs/build-service.md` section "Deployment".
